findings.what: "Textbooks add that 230 V is the rms value" has no footnote and names no textbook (the regulation quote [^1] says only that 230 V is declared, and Calculus fundamentals i10's sources give peak = 1.414 x RMS but never say the mains figure is an RMS value), so an unsourced claim is presented as if it had a source: cite a page that says the declared mains voltage is an RMS value, or label the sentence as unsourced.

findings.where: Screen 5 (Turns a second), freq picture and f slider
findings.what: The graph always spans exactly two turns, so moving Turns a second only relabels the time axis and the picture shows two identical waves at every setting (and the slider thumb jumps from 2 to 50 mid-demonstration with no change to the wave), so the cause, faster turning packing more waves into each second, is told in numbers but never seen: fix the time window, say 1 s or 40 ms, so more turns visibly squeeze in more waves.

findings.where: Screens 9-10 (A head start, Wave B), phi slider and practice.text
findings.what: Only a + phase ever appears (the slider runs 0-360°, every bracket says "slid left", even "slid left 15 ms" at 270°), so the brief's Fiore rule "- if lagging and drawn to the right" is never taught, and screen 10 just repeats screen 9's sentence: let the slider go to -180° with a "slid right" bracket, and ask on screen 10 about an arm started π/2 behind.

Both wrong answers can be ruled out from the picture alone, since -3.1 ms is before the start and 751.5 ms is off a 40 ms axis, while the ringed crossing sits about two-thirds of the way to the 20 ms tick, so the puzzle is passed by elimination; 3.1 ms (sign dropped: 0.979 ÷ 314.16, where the wave reaches +8.3) or 16.9 ms (the second crossing) would test the working instead.
"Move the line to -8.3" asks for something Dan cannot do, because the puzzle has no level-line handle and the line is already drawn there: say "The line is now at -8.3".

findings.where: Screen 1 and every SHOW screen with a live tip (turn1, amp, freq, omega, phase, tan)
findings.what: The draggable tip is only the 3.5-unit tip dot, and its grip is invisible, so the thing to be moved has no visible handle (the level line on screen 11 gets a knob): give the tip a ring or knob like the level line's.
"so it reaches every height a quarter turn sooner" mixes an angle with a time; "a quarter of a turn's time sooner" matches the explain's φ ÷ ω and the "quarter period" in the next sentence.
"UK supplies are declared at 50 Hz, so the axis is then relabelled for 50 Hz" makes a regulation the reason for a relabel; "Now relabel the axis for a UK supply, declared at 50 Hz" reads straight.

findings.where: Whole lesson against brief section 2, lesson 6
findings.what: Three things the brief promised are missing: 60 Hz = 376.99 rad/s and its 16.7 ms period (useful for a marine engineering student, framed as "a college's notes say"), reading the 2πft form directly as in 4 sin(2π5t) = 4 V peak at 5 Hz, and amplitude as Functions' stretch (only the shift is linked back); one line or one option each would cover them.

findings.where: Screen 15 (Where it starts), opening picture at 360 and 1280
findings.what: Before an answer the picture is just an empty circle and empty axes, with no ticks and "time t" floating about 30 px below the axis, so it looks dead: a ringed "?" at t = 0 on the graph's up axis would show where the answer lives without giving it away.

The whole solution (0.5, 0.524, 2.618, 1.67 ms, 8.33 ms) is written into the prose above the picture and then repeated in the rows under it, which makes it the densest block of numbers in the lesson on a phone: keep the idea in the prose and leave the arithmetic to the rows.

The tan graph gets one SHOW screen and no puzzle, and the mixed puzzles never come back to it, so nothing makes it stick: a quick check, such as where the graph has no value or whether tan 135° is positive or negative, would help.
"like a clock's second hand" brings in a hand that turns clockwise, while every arm in the lesson turns anticlockwise: add "though the other way round".
